## Security verdict: PASS WITH NOTES

PR #180, exact head `0ffb88381f6ea11ed6d8816affe2b20b238d7621`.

The complete nine-file PR diff and directly dependent receiver, session, lease and digest boundaries were source-reviewed. No high-confidence new security exploit was identified. This verdict does not certify that every blocked receiver stops renewing within ten minutes.

| # | Severity | File | Lines | Vulnerability | Confidence |
|---|----------|------|-------|---------------|------------|
| - | - | - | - | No new vulnerability identified | - |

### Reinjection and session safety

Queued/in-flight steering and processing return wait before the uncertainty check. Only empty queue plus idle reaches drained history and the independent probe; possible unseen consumption returns false and never authorizes rearm (`.copilot/extensions/pij/store.mjs:1875-1931`).

Recovery repeats the discard check and tests consumption before and after rearm. Exclusive journal intent and per-native-ID retry files prevent competing injection; ambiguous pending transport holds without reinjection or acknowledgement (`store.mjs:721-770,1983-2064`). The new order does not expand the branch that may resend.

Registration is frozen and the SDK session must match the extension context, not merely host ancestry (`store.mjs:1073`; `.copilot/extensions/pij/extension.mjs:114-151`). Durable jobs keep their session target through locked handoff and acknowledgement (`crates/daemon/src/delivery/mod.rs:1970-2037,2241-2311,2624-2657`). Shared turn-owner completion does not confer another logical session's delivery authority.

### Lease qualification

The ten-minute bound applies to the empty-queue/idle/uncertain-discard case only. Queue/in-flight presence bypasses that timer, and independent heartbeats can continue during claim failures (`store.mjs:1225-1237,1275-1359,1880-1931`). Therefore a blanket claim that no lease remains live while claiming is blocked is not proven.

Hard hold aborts receiving and heartbeat renewal; the lease expires after its last renewal's configured window, not immediately. Current-tuple validation prevents an old incarnation renewing its replacement (`crates/daemon/src/delivery/mod.rs:390-426,503-515`). Remaining queueing/health limitations are correctness concerns, not a demonstrated new authority or confidentiality exploit.

### Anomaly rendering and disclosure

The new anomaly is derived from the identity-aware lease map and scoped fleet rows. Detail is fixed daemon text plus numeric duration, not seat-reported diagnostic strings or log contents; no shell/tmux command is built (`crates/daemon/src/pa_watchdog.rs:957-1005,1343-1367`; `crates/core/src/pa_digest.rs:164-179`).

Existing digest interpolation is still unescaped; this is not broader F127 hardening. No new C19/C21 disclosure was identified.

### Proof

GitHub metadata and the independent remote pull ref agree on the full reviewed SHA; GitHub reports CLEAN. CI run `42449058166` and Delivers run `42449058625` both identify this SHA and success.

Regression tests were source-read, not locally executed. No builds, runtime injections, claims, fault injection, credential reads or probes were performed. Exact-head CI is the execution proof; no new live end-to-end session/lease observation is claimed.
